traditions.label: Spirituals
traditions.about: Religious folk songs created by enslaved African Americans, blending African song practice with Christian hymns.

traditions.label: Work songs
traditions.about: Rhythmic group songs sung to coordinate labor, a core form of enslaved African American music.

traditions.label: Field hollers
traditions.about: Solo calls and cries sung by field laborers, ancestors of the blues with origins in West African song.

traditions.label: Ring shout
traditions.about: Circular religious dance of enslaved Africans with clapping, stick-beating and call and response, tied to Kongo ring ceremonies.

traditions.label: Ragtime
traditions.about: Syncopated piano-centred music built on cakewalks, marches and minstrel songs, popularized by Scott Joplin.

traditions.label: Minstrel shows
traditions.about: Racist blackface stage entertainment whose songs and banjo music fed into ragtime, early blues and country.

traditions.label: Brass band and march music
traditions.about: Military-style brass ensembles and marches whose instruments and repertoire shaped New Orleans jazz and ragtime.

listen.title: When the Saints Go Marching In

traditions.label: Christian hymns
traditions.about: Congregational Christian songs, sung in lined-out and shape-note style, that African American spirituals and gospel reworked.

traditions.label: Mento
traditions.about: Jamaican folk music mixing African rhythms with European dance forms; Jamaica's first commercially recorded music.

traditions.label: Kaiso
traditions.about: West and Central African-derived song tradition of enslaved Trinidadians led by a griot-like singer; ancestor of calypso.

traditions.label: Calypso
traditions.about: Topical, rhythmic Trinidadian song style grown from kaiso and canboulay, later spread across the Caribbean.

recording.title: London Is the Place for Me

listen.title: London Is the Place for Me

traditions.label: Kumina
traditions.about: Afro-Jamaican drumming and spirit-possession tradition drawn from Kongo religion, a root of mento.

traditions.label: Junkanoo (Jonkunnu)
traditions.about: Masked drumming and dance festival of enslaved Africans in British Caribbean colonies, with Akan and West African origins.

traditions.label: Son cubano
traditions.about: Eastern Cuban genre blending Spanish guitar-tres song with African rhythm; parent of salsa and Congolese rumba's Cuban influence.

traditions.label: Congolese rumba
traditions.about: Dance music joining Kongo maringa with Cuban son, the foundation of soukous and an input to makossa.

traditions.label: Highlife
traditions.about: Ghanaian dance music fusing palm-wine guitar, Akan music and brass-band sounds; ancestor of Afrobeat and makossa.

traditions.label: Palm-wine music
traditions.region: Coastal West Africa (Sierra Leone, Liberia, Ghana)
traditions.about: Acoustic guitar-and-percussion coastal West African style that fed highlife, with links to kaiso, calypso and mento.

traditions.label: Assiko
traditions.about: Bassa dance music of southern Cameroon, a palm-wine variant that served as the ethnic root of makossa.

traditions.label: Griot (jeli) tradition
traditions.about: Hereditary West African bards who preserve history through song and kora or balafon, said to have shaped talking blues and hip-hop.

traditions.label: West African music

traditions.label: Central African (Kongo and Bantu) music
traditions.about: Bantu and Kongo traditions of Central Africa that shaped Caribbean ritual music, the ring shout and Congolese rumba.

traditions.label: Traditional music of Africa
traditions.about: Oral, rhythm-centred African musical traditions built on drums, polyrhythm and call and response.

traditions.label: Prehistoric music
